sentences.text:
Having considered the submissions of the parties noted above, finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant, keeping in view the uncertainty regarding conclusion of trial; one sided investigation by police, ignoring the case of accused side; applicant being under-trial having fundamental right to speedy trial; larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil Vs.
C.B.I. & Another, passed in S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, judgement dated 11.7.2022 and considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the applicant involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions that :-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

Author: Siddharth

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:AHC:217779 Court No. - 64 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 48633 of 2023 Applicant :- Vikas Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anil Kumar Bind Hon'ble Siddharth,J.

opennyai_summary.16_November_2023__facts:
There is allegation against the applicant of abduction of a major woman.
In FIR, subsequently,
allegations of committing the offences of rape and criminal intimidation has also been leveled against the applicant.
Thereafter, she lodged FIR.
opennyai_summary.16_November_2023__arguments:
She eloped with the applicant and lived with him.
The victim has given application before police stating that she was living with the applicant in live-in relationship.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has no criminal history to his credit and is languishing in jail since 16.08.2023.
Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the victim has never given any such application before police that she was living in live-in relationship with applicant.
In case the applicant is released on bail, he will indulge in similar activities and will misuse the liberty of bail.
opennyai_summary.16_November_2023__ANALYSIS:
Having considered the submissions of the parties noted above, finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant, keeping in view the uncertainty regarding conclusion of trial; one sided investigation by police, ignoring the case of accused side; applicant being under-trial having fundamental right to speedy trial; larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil Vs.
C.B.I. & Another, passed in S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, judgement dated 11.7.2022 and considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the applicant involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions that :-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
opennyai_summary.16_November_2023__decision:
(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or as directed by the Court.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) In case the applicant misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement Vikas vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171323478/
2 under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
The court below is directed to conclude the trial against the applicant, as expeditiously as possible,
preferably within a period of one year.
Registrar(Compliance) is directed to communicate this order to the concerned court below within ten days.

opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant and the victim were in consensual relationship.
In this regard, reliance has been placed on the report dated 19.09.2022 submitted by the Assistant Commissioner of Police-3 Central Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar, pursuant to the complaint filed by the victim before the registration of the FIR.
The applicant is a Class-III employee in the Indian Air Force.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
No custodial interrogation is required.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest in the above mentioned case.
8. Having regard to the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, in particular the fact that the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. has been filed after inordinate delay, the fact that the report dated 19.09.2024 submitted by the Assistant Commissioner of Police-3 Central Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar states that the applicant and the victim were in consensual relationship, the fact that the applicant had cooperated in the investigation and no custodial interrogation is required, the fact that no adverse material has been produced by learned AGA, which may warrant any modification of the earlier orders passed by this Court, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
